docs.title: Augmented row-column design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_augmented_row_column.R

Arrange unreplicated test entries and k replicated checks in a complete rectangular field, so that every check appears exactly once in every field line along check_direction, and search the check positions for an efficient design under fixed row and column effects.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
augmented_row_column(
  nrows,
  ncols,
  checks,
  check_direction,
  entries = NULL,
  objective = arc_design_defaults()$objective,
  method = "staged",
  budget = NULL,
  time_limit = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  planter = "serpentine",
  locationNames = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  data = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: nrows Number of field rows, a whole number. ncols Number of field columns, a whole number. checks The checks: a whole-number count k >= 2, which gives the labels CH1, ..., CHk, or a character vector of at least two distinct, nonmissing, nonblank labels, used in that order. With data, it must be the count of checks. check_direction "columns" or "rows": the physical direction along which every check appears once per line. Required, with no default; it is never inferred from the field shape. With "columns", each check appears once in every field column, so v = nrows and s = ncols; with "rows", once in every field row, so v = ncols and s = nrows. The design needs s <= v. entries The test entries, excluding checks. NULL (default) fills every test plot, nrows * ncols - k * s of them, with the labels G(k+1), ..., G(k+n). A whole-number count must equal that number of test plots and gives the same labels. A character vector of distinct, nonmissing, nonblank labels must have that length. Must be NULL when data is given. objective The criterion the search optimizes: "V_tt" (minimize the mean variance of test-versus-test comparisons), "V_tc" (minimize the mean variance of test-versus-check comparisons) or "E_aug" (maximize the harmonic-mean efficiency of all treatment comparisons). The default is "V_tt". Pass objective explicitly when a result must be reproducible across package versions; reproduction code always states it. method Search method. Only "staged" (staged annealing with recolouring restarts) is available. budget Objective-function calls allowed per location, a positive whole number. NULL (default) uses 60,000 calls when v * s <= 600 and 100,000 above. Pass budget explicitly when a result must be reproducible across package versions. The recorded parameters keep the effective value. time_limit Optional per-location search cutoff, in seconds of wall-clock time, or NULL (default) for none. See "Search, budget and time limit" below. l Number of locations, each an independent run of the same search. plotNumber First plot number: one positive whole number, used at every location, or one per location. planter Plot-number path, "serpentine" or "cartesian". locationNames Distinct nonblank location labels, one per location; NULL gives 1, ..., l. exptName Experiment name recorded in the EXPT column; NULL gives "Expt1". year Year recorded in the YEAR column; NULL gives the current calendar year. The effective year is recorded, so a later replay reproduces it. seed Randomization seed; NULL draws and records one automatic seed. data Optional entry table with exactly the columns ENTRY and NAME, as in diagonal_arrangement(): the first checks rows are the checks and the remaining rows the tests. ENTRY holds distinct positive whole numbers and NAME distinct, nonblank text labels. It must have k rows plus one row per test plot.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A schema-1 FielDHub result with class fieldhub_augmented_row_column and the elements:

  • infoDesign: nrows, ncols, check_direction, the mathematical v, s and k, the check labels checks, the test count entries, locations, locationNames, residual_df, objective, method, the effective budget, seed and id_design.

  • fieldBook: ID, EXPT, LOCATION, YEAR, PLOT, ROW, COLUMN, CHECKS, ENTRY, TREATMENT and CHECK_DIRECTION. ROW and COLUMN are physical field coordinates; CHECKS is the check's ENTRY on check plots and 0 on test plots; TREATMENT is the label, unchanged.

  • statistics: one row per location with LOCATION, E_aug, V_tt, V_tc, V_cc, max_tt, max_tc, residual_df, authority and lambda_min_rel, from the final scoring of the returned placement.

  • diagnostics: per location, the location and its seed, the search status and phase statuses, objective and proxy calls, proposals, failed proposals, disconnected candidates and time_limit_hit.

  • contraction: per location, the k x s matrix whose entry (h, j) is the cross-line holding check h in field line j (field column j for "columns", field row j for "rows"), with rows in check-label order.

  • timing: per location, search, verification and total elapsed seconds, kept apart from the deterministic content.

  • metadata: the seed, RNG settings, package version and the complete effective parameters.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Construction. The design is a complete nrows x ncols field. Every test entry occupies one plot and every check occupies s plots: exactly one in each of the s field lines along check_direction. Along the v cross-lines, no check is repeated and every cross-line holds between floor(k * s / v) and ceiling(k * s / v) check plots, at least one. This is the restricted contraction construction of Piepho and Williams (2026); square fields (v = s) include the square-array designs of Bailey and Haines (2025). Field coordinates and plot numbers are fixed at construction.

Model and objectives. Under the additive model with fixed row, column and entry effects and independent errors, the residual degrees of freedom are k * s - k - v - s + 2. Fields with fewer than 1 are rejected. Fields with fewer than 10 raise a warning: only adding a check or changing the number of rows or columns raises them. E_aug, V_tt and V_tc are reported for every location, whichever is optimized.

Search, budget and time limit. FielDHub searches the check positions with staged annealing; the search is FielDHub's own method, not part of the published construction. Each location runs one search with its own seed (the recorded seed plus the location index minus one) and at most budget objective calls. time_limit, when given, bounds each location's search phase only: final verification, randomization and field-book assembly always run to completion, and with l locations the call can take about l * time_limit seconds plus that work. A location stopped by the time limit records time_limit_hit = TRUE in its diagnostics. A cutoff reached before the search has produced any design raises a fieldhub_arc_search_error, as does a search that finds no connected start; there is no silent fallback to another method.

Randomization. After the search, the field lines and cross-lines are permuted at random, the check labels receive one random permutation, and the tests are assigned to the test plots at random. None of these steps changes an objective. The returned contraction and statistics describe this final, randomized placement.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
reproduce_design(x) and do.call(augmented_row_column, x$metadata$parameters) replay the design from its recorded parameters. Replay is exact (identical field book, contraction, statistics, diagnostics and parameters; only timing and the recorded package version are excluded) for evaluation-budget runs that did not hit time_limit, within the same software and numerical environment: the same FielDHub and R versions, BLAS/LAPACK library and thread count, and platform. A time_limit cutoff makes replay timing-dependent. In a different environment, replay gives a valid design with comparable statistics, which may be a different design.

Standalone reproduction code is available for the standard entry template at any size, and for any upload up to 200 rows. An upload whose ENTRY values are exactly 1, ..., k + n in row order is recorded as its check and test labels, with data = NULL; other uploads are recorded as uploaded, and above 200 rows the reproduction code falls back to the saved result (RDS).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Piepho, H.-P., and Williams, E. R. (2026). Rectangular augmented row-column designs generated from contractions. Biometrical Journal, 68(5), e70182. doi:10.1002/bimj.70182

Bailey, R. A., and Haines, L. M. (2025). Square array designs for unreplicated test treatments with replicated controls. Journal of Agricultural, Biological and Environmental Statistics. doi:10.1007/s13253-025-00699-1

docs.title: See also
docs.text: diagonal_arrangement, reproduce_design, design_arguments

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# 4 checks and 48 tests in a 10 x 8 field; every check appears once in
# each field column. A small budget keeps the example fast.
x <- augmented_row_column(nrows = 10, ncols = 8, checks = 4,
                          check_direction = "columns", budget = 2000,
                          seed = 2026)
x$infoDesign$residual_df
#> [1] 12
x$statistics
#>   LOCATION     E_aug     V_tt     V_tc      V_cc   max_tt   max_tc residual_df
#> 1        1 0.5884851 3.502748 1.872188 0.2767563 4.120002 2.037172          12
#>     authority lambda_min_rel
#> 1 full_layout      0.1722068
head(x$fieldBook)
#>   ID  EXPT LOCATION YEAR PLOT ROW COLUMN CHECKS ENTRY TREATMENT CHECK_DIRECTION
#> 1  1 Expt1        1 2026  101   1      1      0     7        G7         columns
#> 2  2 Expt1        1 2026  102   1      2      3     3       CH3         columns
#> 3  3 Expt1        1 2026  103   1      3      1     1       CH1         columns
#> 4  4 Expt1        1 2026  104   1      4      4     4       CH4         columns
#> 5  5 Expt1        1 2026  105   1      5      0    30       G30         columns
#> 6  6 Expt1        1 2026  106   1      6      0     8        G8         columns
# Check plots per field column: each check once in every column
checks <- x$fieldBook[x$fieldBook$CHECKS > 0, ]
table(checks$TREATMENT, checks$COLUMN)
#>      
#>       1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
#>   CH1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH2 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH3 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1
#>   CH4 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1

# The same field turned through 90 degrees, with labelled checks
y <- augmented_row_column(nrows = 8, ncols = 10,
                          checks = c("Check A", "Check B", "Check C",
                                     "Check D"),
                          check_direction = "rows", objective = "E_aug",
                          budget = 2000, seed = 7)
y$contraction
#> $`1`
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8]
#> [1,]   10    7    5    9    6    1    2    8
#> [2,]    8    3    9    6    4    2    5    7
#> [3,]    2   10    1    7    5    8    3    4
#> [4,]    9    1    4    3   10    6    8    2
#> 

# Replay from the recorded parameters
identical(reproduce_design(x)$fieldBook, x$fieldBook)
#> [1] TRUE

docs.title: Shared design arguments and compatibility
docs.text:
Source: R/api_vocabulary.R

Use named arguments when writing FielDHub scripts. The common names below describe the same concepts across the design families that support them. Each function's help page defines its supported inputs and constraints.

docs.title: Common arguments
docs.text: t Treatments in classical designs: a count or, where supported, a vector of labels. Check-based designs use lines for the number of experimental entries excluding checks. entries Test entries excluding checks, as a count or as a vector of labels, in augmented_row_column(). It describes the same entries as lines in the other check-based designs, where lines is a count only; entries also accepts labels because an uploaded entry list is recorded portably as its labels. reps Full replicates per location in classical, incomplete-block, lattice, row-column and strip-plot designs. In latin_square(), this is the number of independent squares. Partial and multi-location replication uses the design-specific allocation arguments instead. l Number of locations. CRD() and latin_square() generate one location and have no l argument. locationNames Location labels, in location order. CRD() takes one location name. plotNumber Starting plot number, or one start per location. seed Seed recorded in the result to reproduce randomization. When seed is NULL, one integer is drawn from the current random-number stream and recorded; the design's own randomization does not change the caller's stream. k Number of plots per incomplete block. checks A check count, entry identifiers, or labels; see "Dimensions, factors and checks" below. rep_checks Check replication: how many times each check is repeated. RCBD() takes one count per check label supplied in checks (recycled from a scalar). optimized_arrangement() takes either a total check count or one count per check label (this is amountChecks in 1.5.x scripts; see "Migrating existing scripts"). Multi-location allocations (multi_location_prep(), do_optim(design = "prep")) take the same one-count-per-check form. sparse_allocation() and do_optim(design = "sparse") have no rep_checks: every check is replicated once per location by construction.

docs.title: Dimensions, factors and checks
docs.text:
nrows and ncols describe field dimensions in spatial designs. In row_column(), nrows is the number of rows per replicate; field_layout() controls how replicates are placed in the field. Factorial, split-plot and strip-plot designs keep their factor-specific arguments so whole plots, subplots and crossed strips remain distinct. The meaning of checks is design-specific: a count, entry identifiers, or labels. Consult the function's help before transferring a check vector between design families.

Partial and multi-location replication does not share one argument name across families; each keeps the allocation arguments that describe its own replication scheme: partially_replicated()'s repGens (how many entries get each replication level) and repUnits (those replication levels), and RCBD_augmented()'s b (number of augmented blocks) and repsExpt (replicates of the whole experiment). These are design-specific allocation arguments, not aliases of reps or rep_checks.

docs.title: Boolean controls
docs.text: Logical switches such as continuous, factorLabels, spread_reps, allow_fillers, and randomizeH require one nonmissing TRUE or FALSE. Numeric switches (0/1), strings, vectors, and arrays are not supported. Invalid switches signal a fieldhub_input_error before randomization, with argument, value, and options fields identifying the correction.

docs.title: Migrating existing scripts
docs.text:
CRD(locationName = ...) remains supported; use CRD(locationNames = ...) in new code. In incomplete_blocks(), alpha_lattice(), square_lattice(), rectangular_lattice() and row_column(), replace the argument name r with reps. In strip_plot(), replace b with reps. In optimized_arrangement(), replace amountChecks with rep_checks. RCBD_augmented(b = ...) still denotes blocks and is unchanged.

Old names and positional calls retain their meaning and signal a warning of class fieldhub_deprecated_warning. Supplying both names for one argument is an error, even if their values agree. These aliases do not change seeded designs or the field names of saved results.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: CRD, incomplete_blocks, row_column, strip_plot, field_layout

docs.title: Supported recorded-design file formats
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_design_formats.R

Lists the version and read/write capabilities of the built-in design format registry. Formats are selected explicitly, not guessed from filenames. CSV tables and app workflow ZIPs are separate exports; neither is silently interpreted as a complete recorded design by these functions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: design_formats()

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A data frame with format, extension, media_type, format_version, readable and writable columns.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
design_formats()
#>   format extension               media_type format_version readable writable
#> 1    rds       rds application/octet-stream              1     TRUE     TRUE
#> 2      r         R               text/plain              1    FALSE     TRUE

docs.title: Design results and reproducibility metadata
docs.text:
Source: R/api_result_contract.R

FielDHub uses a versioned result contract. Schema 1 retains the established elements and storage types of each design family; validation checks those elements without coercing valid field books or removing user columns. Field, family, allocation and optimization results share the same construction boundary, with validation appropriate to each result type.

docs.title: Field designs
docs.text:
Field designs inherit from FielDHub, with a first class such as fieldhub_rcbd identifying the engine. Test inheritance with inherits(x, "FielDHub"), not equality with class(x). Their fieldBook contains finite numeric ID and PLOT vectors and nonmissing atomic LOCATION identifiers. Integer and double storage, factors, and the existing character or numeric location conventions are preserved rather than normalized.

Additional required columns depend on the design:

  • CRD and RCBD: REP, TREATMENT. RCBD with repeated checks also requires ENTRY and CHECKS.

  • Latin square: SQUARE, ROW, COLUMN, TREATMENT.

  • Factorial: REP, TRT_COMB, and one FACTOR_<name> column per recorded factor.

  • Split plot: REP, WHOLE_PLOT, SUB_PLOT, TRT_COMB; split-split plot also requires SUB_SUB_PLOT.

  • Strip plot: REP, HSTRIP, VSTRIP, TRT_COMB.

  • Incomplete blocks and lattices: REP, IBLOCK, UNIT, ENTRY, TREATMENT.

  • Row-column: REP, ROW, COLUMN, ENTRY, TREATMENT.

  • Diagonal, optimized, sparse, augmented and partially replicated: EXPT, YEAR, ROW, COLUMN, CHECKS, ENTRY, TREATMENT. Augmented RCBD adds BLOCK; partially replicated designs add REP.

Required extension columns are atomic vectors, not matrix or list columns. Numeric values must be finite. Missing CHECKS values remain supported, as do missing REP values on partially replicated filler plots with ENTRY = 0. Other required extension values cannot be missing. Extra columns are permitted. Use field_layout() to obtain the final coordinates and plot numbers for a chosen planting path and layout.

docs.title: Family splits and allocation plans
docs.text:
split_families() returns rowsEachlist with location counts and data_locations with ENTRY, NAME, FAMILY and LOCATION. Counts must agree with the entry table, including locations with zero entries.

do_optim() retains the Sparse or MultiPrep class. Its allocation counts, location sizes and entry lists are validated; these plans are not field books and do not yet specify plot coordinates.

docs.title: Standalone optimization
docs.text: swap_pairs() retains its matrices, distances and stopping diagnostics, with the classes fieldhub_pair_swap and fieldhub_optimization. Its shared metadata includes the input matrix and every optimization control. The validator checks field geometry, entry counts and retained search steps. These results can be saved and replayed with reproduce_design().

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
metadata records design, schema_version, seed, rng_kind, package_version and, in newly generated results, parameters. Parameters use effective values after validation, including defaults, the resolved year and seed, and uploaded data. Automatic seeds are integers; explicit real-valued seeds retain the legacy behavior of R's set.seed(), which truncates to an integer.

Use saveRDS() and readRDS() to retain the exact result and its metadata, then reproduce_design() to reconstruct it. Exact replay of optimization may require the same dependency versions and platform. Layout selections and simulated responses added later by the app are not part of the core design parameters.

Older schema-1 metadata without parameters still validates, but cannot be replayed automatically. Objects saved by FielDHub 1.5.0 without metadata remain supported by the print, summary and plotting compatibility methods; they are not silently rewritten to the new schema.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: reproduce_design, field_layout, design_arguments

docs.title: Spatial Un-replicated Diagonal Arrangement Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_diagonal_arrangement.R

Randomly generates an spatial un-replicated diagonal arrangement design.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
diagonal_arrangement(
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  lines = NULL,
  checks = NULL,
  planter = "serpentine",
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  kindExpt = "SUDC",
  splitBy = "row",
  seed = NULL,
  blocks = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  multiLocationData = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  checksPercent = NULL,
  sameEntries = FALSE,
  spread_checks = FALSE,
  dist_method = "euclidean"
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: nrows Number of rows in the field. ncols Number of columns in the field. lines Number of genotypes, experimental lines or treatments. checks Number of genotypes checks, or a vector of their entry numbers (distinct consecutive whole numbers in increasing order, e.g. c(301, 302)). planter Option for serpentine or cartesian plot arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. l Number of locations or sites. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. kindExpt Type of diagonal design, with single options: Single Un-replicated Diagonal Checks 'SUDC' and Decision Blocks Un-replicated Design with Diagonal Checks 'DBUDC' for multiple experiments. By default kindExpt = 'SUDC'. splitBy Option to split the field when kindExpt = 'DBUDC' is selected. By default splitBy = 'row'. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. blocks Number of experiments or blocks to generate an DBUDC design. If kindExpt = 'DBUDC' and data is null, blocks are mandatory. exptName (optional) Name of the experiment. locationNames (optional) Names each location. multiLocationData (optional) Option to pass an entry list for multiple locations. By default multiLocationData = FALSE. data (optional) Data frame with 2 columns: ENTRY | NAME. year (optional) Year recorded in the YEAR column of the field book. By default the current year. checksPercent (optional) Percentage of checks, one of the options available for the field dimensions. By default the last (largest) option. sameEntries (optional) Logical. When TRUE and kindExpt = "DBUDC", every block holds the same entries, and all blocks must have the same size. By default sameEntries = FALSE. spread_checks Logical. Exchange check identities among the existing check plots of each location to increase separation of repeated checks, for kindExpt = "SUDC" and "DBUDC". Test entries, filler plots, the check plots themselves, the experiments (blocks) and each check's replication in the location stay fixed. The default FALSE preserves the original randomization. dist_method Distance between field coordinates for check optimization: "euclidean" (default) or "manhattan". Grid steps have equal scale.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A FielDHub design result with the following components.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters. With check optimization enabled, check_optimization records swaps, candidate evaluations, stopping reason and minimum distance before and after optimization for each location.

  • check_spacing records per-check minimum, mean nearest and mean pairwise distances, and same-check neighbors within 5 grid steps, for each location. With optimization enabled, both the original and final assignments are recorded. print() shows the spacing overview and summary() adds per-check details without rerunning the optimizer. Distances use dist_method and equally scaled row/column coordinates, not physical plot dimensions. Overall distances average equally across checks with repeated occurrences; neighbor percentages include all check occurrences. These metrics measure spacing, not statistical precision.

  • layoutRandom is a matrix with the randomization layout.

  • plotsNumber is a matrix with the layout plot number.

  • data_entry is a data frame with the data input.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with field book design. This includes the index (Row, Column).

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Check optimization compares counts of same-check pairs at ascending distances, reducing the count at the shortest differing distance first. It is a deterministic local exchange heuristic, not a statistical-efficiency or global-optimality guarantee. Each location stops after a complete scan finds no improvement, 100 accepted swaps, or 100,000 candidate evaluations. One check identity, or checks occurring only once, leaves the layout unchanged. With kindExpt = "DBUDC" identities are exchanged across the whole field of a location, as for a single arrangement: the entries and the plots of every experiment stay where they are. The selected check percentage and filler count are unchanged. With checksPercent = NULL, Single Diagonal Arrangement still selects the valid option with the most check plots and therefore the fewest fillers.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(diagonal_arrangement, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Clarke, G. P. Y., & Stefanova, K. T. (2011). Optimal design for early-generation plant breeding trials with unreplicated or partially replicated test lines. Australian & New Zealand Journal of Statistics, 53(4), 461–480.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Generate the sparse or p-rep allocation to multiple locations.
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_do_optim.R

Generate the sparse or p-rep allocation to multiple locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
do_optim(
  design = "sparse",
  lines,
  l,
  copies_per_entry,
  add_checks = FALSE,
  checks = NULL,
  rep_checks = NULL,
  force_balance = TRUE,
  seed,
  data = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: design Type of experimental design. It can be prep or sparse lines Number of genotypes, experimental lines or treatments. l Number of locations or sites. By default l = 1. copies_per_entry Number of copies per plant. When design is sparse then copies_per_entry should be less than l add_checks Option to add checks. Optional if design = "prep" checks Number of genotypes checks. rep_checks Replication for each check. force_balance Get balanced unbalanced locations. By default force_balance = TRUE. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. data (optional) Data frame with 2 columns: ENTRY | NAME. ENTRY must be numeric.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with five elements, classed c("fieldhub_sparse_optimization", "Sparse") or c("fieldhub_multi_prep_optimization", "MultiPrep"): the legacy Sparse/MultiPrep class is retained for compatibility, with an additional fieldhub_* class alongside it.

  • multi_location_data is a data frame with the entries of every location: LOCATION | ENTRY | NAME, with a REPS column for p-rep allocations.

  • list_locs is a list with each location list of entries.

  • allocation is a data frame of test-entry copy counts, with one column per location.

  • size_locations is a named vector of test-entry copies per location, excluding checks.

  • metadata records the allocation type, schema version, seed, random-number settings, package version and evaluated input parameters. With the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild the allocation with do.call(do_optim, x$metadata$parameters). Its allocation_search element records how the search ended: stop_reason, evaluations and even_repairs.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The entry copies are allocated to the locations by FielDHub's own compiled block-design search: D-optimal plot swaps after Edmondson (2020), 20 searches from random starts drawn with the seed (the first starts from a square lattice when the shape is one). Every allocation is even: each entry has floor(copies_per_entry / l) or one more copies at each location (a final even-up step guarantees it), and location totals differ by at most one copy before force_balance. One location takes every copy without a search. From FielDHub 1.7.0 this search replaces blocksdesign::blocks(), so allocations for a given seed differ from earlier versions.

The swap search stops after at most 60 seconds; the even-up step and the final scoring run after it, outside that limit. A run stopped by the limit warns, records stop_reason = "time_limit", and may not be reproducible from its seed, because where it stopped depends on the machine's speed.

docs.title: References
docs.text: Edmondson, R.N. Multi-level Block Designs for Comparative Experiments. JABES 25, 500–522 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1007/s13253-020-00416-0

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
sparse_example <- do_optim(
   design = "sparse",
   lines = 120,
   l = 4,
   copies_per_entry = 3,
   add_checks = TRUE,
   checks = 4,
   seed = 15
)

docs.title: Field layout of a design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_field_layout.R

Returns the field book of a design with the ROW and COLUMN of every plot, for the layout, planter and stacking chosen. This is the field book that plot() draws and that the app exports.

The field books of CRD(), RCBD(), latin_square(), full_factorial(), split_plot(), split_split_plot(), strip_plot(), incomplete_blocks(), row_column() and the lattice designs have no field coordinates by default: their plots can be arranged in several ways, and the layouts that renumber the plots along the planting path also change PLOT. The other designs place their plots when they are built; their field book already has ROW and COLUMN, and it is returned as it is. The physical layout of a resolvable row-column design retains the experimental axes as ROW_REP and COLUMN_REP.

With nrows or ncols, the design is placed in a field of those dimensions instead of a numbered layout. Each location must have exactly as many cells as plots, including repeated checks, and the units of the design are equal rectangles of the field:

  • CRD and factorials in CRD fill any rectangle that holds the plots.

  • RCBD and factorials in RCBD keep each complete block together.

  • Incomplete blocks and lattices keep each replicate and each incomplete block together.

  • Split plots keep each whole plot together, split-split plots also each subplot, and their RCBD variants each replicate.

  • Latin squares and strip plots tile their squares and strip grids whole, in their own orientation. The row and column labels of a Latin square are kept as ROW_SQ and COLUMN_SQ.

The plots are then numbered along the planting path of the whole field, serpentine or cartesian as planter says, as in the numbered layouts: the plot numbers of the location are handed out in increasing order as the planter reaches each plot, and the path does not restart in each block or replicate. With a serpentine planter, consecutive plot numbers are therefore neighbours in the field. Subplots that share a plot number keep sharing one; whole plots that tile the field as equal rectangles are numbered along the planter's path over the grid of whole plots, so consecutive whole plots are neighbours too. The randomization does not change: every row of the field book keeps its treatment, replicate and block, and only PLOT differs from the design's own field book. Where the plot numbers restart at each replicate (101, 201, ...), the hundreds name the replicate only where the replicates lie one above the other.

In a field of given dimensions, stacked arranges the replicates: the complete blocks of an RCBD or of a factorial in blocks, the replicates of split, split-split and strip plots, of incomplete blocks and of the lattices, and the squares of a Latin square.

  • "vertical": one above another. Each replicate spans all the columns of the field and nrows / reps of its rows.

  • "horizontal": side by side. Each replicate spans all the rows of the field and ncols / reps of its columns.

  • "grid_panel": in rows and columns of replicates, more than one of each.

When stacked is not given with dimensions, the stacking is the one whose replicate is the most square (the smallest difference between its rows and its columns) among those that fit the dimensions; this also chooses among the panels of "grid_panel". A tie goes to "vertical", then to "horizontal", then to the panel with the most rows of replicates. CRD, and factorials and split plots in CRD, have no replicates to stack: stacked with their dimensions is an error.

Dimensions that do not fit, or do not fit the stacking asked for, are an error that suggests dimensions that do. layout selects a numbered layout: giving it together with dimensions is an error.

A design built with dimensions (RCBD(..., nrows = 4)) has one layout: the grid stored in its field book, numbered along the path of the planter it was built with, its replicates stacked as its metadata$parameters$stacked records. field_layout() returns that field book when it is called with no other argument, or with the same planter, stacked or dimensions. Another planter, another stacked or other dimensions are an error: for another layout, build the design again with other dimensions or another stacking, or without dimensions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
field_layout(
  x,
  layout = 1,
  planter = "serpentine",
  stacked = "vertical",
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: x A design created by a FielDHub function. layout Layout option, a whole number. The options depend on the design, the planter and the stacking; an unavailable option is an error that lists the available ones. planter Order in which the plots are planted: "serpentine" (by default) or "cartesian". stacked How the reps are arranged: "vertical" (by default), "horizontal", or "grid_panel" for designs in incomplete blocks and split plots in complete blocks with more than two reps. With nrows or ncols it arranges the replicates in the field of those dimensions, for every design with replicates, and its default is the stacking whose replicate is the most square (see the description). nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location, for the designs listed above. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A data frame: the field book of every location with the columns ID, LOCATION, PLOT, ROW and COLUMN first.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
rcbd <- RCBD(t = 6, reps = 3, plotNumber = 101, seed = 1)
head(field_layout(rcbd))
#>   ID LOCATION PLOT ROW COLUMN REP TREATMENT
#> 1  1     loc1  101   1      1   1        T1
#> 2  2     loc1  102   1      2   1        T4
#> 3  3     loc1  103   1      3   1        T3
#> 4  4     loc1  104   1      4   1        T6
#> 5  5     loc1  105   1      5   1        T2
#> 6  6     loc1  106   1      6   1        T5
# Blocks side by side, plots planted row by row
head(field_layout(rcbd, stacked = "horizontal", planter = "cartesian"))
#>   ID LOCATION PLOT ROW COLUMN REP TREATMENT
#> 1  1     loc1  101   1      1   1        T1
#> 2  2     loc1  102   2      1   1        T4
#> 3  3     loc1  103   3      1   1        T3
#> 4  4     loc1  104   4      1   1        T6
#> 5  5     loc1  105   5      1   1        T2
#> 6  6     loc1  106   6      1   1        T5
# Six complete blocks arranged two down and three across in a field of
# 4 rows and 9 columns, numbered along the serpentine path of the field

docs.title: Generates a Full Factorial Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_full_factorial.R

It randomly generates a full factorial design across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
full_factorial(
  setfactors = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  l = 1,
  type = 2,
  plotNumber = 101,
  continuous = FALSE,
  planter = "serpentine",
  seed = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  factorLabels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: setfactors Numeric vector with levels of each factor. reps Number of replicates (full blocks). l Number of locations. By default l = 1. type Option for CRD or RCBD designs. Values are type = 1 (CRD) or type = 2 (RCBD). By default type = 2. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. continuous Logical for plot number continuous or not. By default continuous = FALSE. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian plot arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. factorLabels (optional) If TRUE retain the levels labels from the original data set otherwise, numeric labels will be assigned. Default is factorLabels =TRUE. data (optional) Data frame whose first two columns contain factor names and level labels. Levels must be unique within each factor, but a label may occur in different factors. Incomplete rows are omitted. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the planting path of the whole field (see planter). See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout. An error for type = 1, which has no replicates to stack.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the full factorial field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(full_factorial, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Federer, W. T. (1955). Experimental Design. Theory and Application. New York, USA. The Macmillan Company.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Generates a Resolvable Incomplete Block Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_incomplete_blocks.R

Randomly generates a resolvable incomplete block design (IBD) of characteristics (t, k, r). The randomization can be done across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
incomplete_blocks(
  t = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  locationNames = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments, or a character vector with the treatment labels. k Size of incomplete blocks (number of units per incomplete block). r Deprecated alias for reps; positional calls remain supported. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. reps Number of full resolvable replicates per location. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the serpentine planting path of the whole field. See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the incomplete block design field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters, using reps for replication. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(incomplete_blocks, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: Randomized cyclic Latin rectangle
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_latin_rectangle.R

Arrange treatments in fewer complete rows than a Latin square, with no treatment repeated in any column. Each row is a complete replicate.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
latin_rectangle(
  t,
  rows = 3,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  planter = "serpentine",
  seed = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments (at least two), or distinct character labels. rows Number of complete rows, from two through the treatment count. l Number of independently randomized locations. plotNumber First plot number: one positive whole number, or one per location. Plot numbers restart at the supplied value for each location. planter Plot-number traversal, "serpentine" or "cartesian". seed Randomization seed; NULL draws and records one automatic seed. locationNames Distinct nonblank location labels, one per location; NULL generates LOC1, LOC2, and so on. Labels are preserved.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A schema-1 FielDHub result with infoDesign, a field book containing ID, LOCATION, PLOT, ROW, COLUMN, REP and TREATMENT, and replay metadata. REP is the complete row block. Use reproduce_design() for replay and field_layout() for the recorded coordinates.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The construction takes the first rows consecutive shifts of the cyclic Latin square, then independently permutes rows, columns and treatment labels at each location. It samples this cyclic construction family, not uniformly from all Latin rectangles, and does not optimize efficiency. It uses O(l * rows * t) construction work with no search.

Rows are complete blocks; columns are incomplete when rows < t. This is not necessarily a balanced incomplete-block or Youden design. Consecutive cyclic shifts keep the additive row/column/treatment model connected. Its residual degrees of freedom at one location are (rows - 2) * (t - 1): two-row rectangles are saturated and cannot independently estimate residual variation under that model. Interactions are not separately estimable. Choose replication and analysis with the intended scientific use in mind.

Field coordinates and plot numbering are fixed at construction. The planter and stacked arguments to field_layout() do not rearrange a saved rectangle. Supplied seeds preserve the caller's RNG; an automatic seed consumes exactly one recorded draw.

docs.title: References
docs.text: Peter G. Doyle, The number of Latin rectangles. https://math.dartmouth.edu/~doyle/docs/latin/latin.pdf.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
x <- latin_rectangle(t = 5, rows = 3, seed = 27)
x$fieldBook
#>    ID LOCATION PLOT ROW COLUMN REP TREATMENT
#> 1   1     LOC1  101   1      1   1        T1
#> 2   2     LOC1  102   1      2   1        T3
#> 3   3     LOC1  103   1      3   1        T4
#> 4   4     LOC1  104   1      4   1        T5
#> 5   5     LOC1  105   1      5   1        T2
#> 6   6     LOC1  106   2      5   2        T1
#> 7   7     LOC1  107   2      4   2        T4
#> 8   8     LOC1  108   2      3   2        T3
#> 9   9     LOC1  109   2      2   2        T2
#> 10 10     LOC1  110   2      1   2        T5
#> 11 11     LOC1  111   3      1   3        T4
#> 12 12     LOC1  112   3      2   3        T1
#> 13 13     LOC1  113   3      3   3        T2
#> 14 14     LOC1  114   3      4   3        T3
#> 15 15     LOC1  115   3      5   3        T5
identical(reproduce_design(x), x)
#> [1] TRUE

docs.title: Generates a Latin Square Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_latin_square.R

Randomly generates a latin square design of up 10 treatments.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
latin_square(
  t = NULL,
  reps = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  planter = "serpentine",
  seed = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments. reps Number of full resolvable squares. By default reps = 1. plotNumber Starting plot number. By default plotNumber = 101. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. locationNames (optional) Name for the location. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the planting path of the whole field (see planter). See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the squares of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of squares). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose square is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with information on the design parameters.

Data frame with the latin square field book.

A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the latin square field book.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: The randomized search is limited to 100,000 placement iterations per square. If it cannot complete a square within that budget, it raises a fieldhub_search_error with the square number and iteration limit. No incomplete design is returned; try a different seed. Designs completed within the limit retain their existing seeded output.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(latin_square, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Federer, W. T. (1955). Experimental Design. Theory and Application. New York, USA. The Macmillan Company.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Thiago de Paula Oliveira[ctb] Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Optimized multi-location partially replicated design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_multi_location_prep.R

Optimized multi-location partially replicated design

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
multi_location_prep(
  lines,
  nrows,
  ncols,
  l,
  planter = "serpentine",
  plotNumber,
  desired_avg,
  copies_per_entry,
  checks = NULL,
  rep_checks = NULL,
  exptName,
  locationNames,
  optim_list,
  seed,
  spread_reps = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  allow_fillers = FALSE,
  max_fillers = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  rowcol_penalty = 0,
  rowcol_scope = "pairs"
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: lines Number of genotypes, experimental lines or treatments. nrows Numeric vector with the number of rows field at each location. ncols Numeric vector with the number of columns field at each location. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian movement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. desired_avg (optional) Desired average of treatments across locations. copies_per_entry Number of total copies per treatment. checks Number of checks. rep_checks Number of replications per check. exptName (optional) Name of the experiment. locationNames (optional) Name for each location. optim_list (optional) A list object of class "MultiPrep"generated by do_optim() function. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. spread_reps A logical value indicating whether to maximize the spatial distance between replicated treatments in the field. Default is TRUE. data (optional) Data frame with 2 columns: ENTRY | NAME. ENTRY must be numeric. allow_fillers A logical value indicating whether field dimensions may exceed the number of experimental plots. Fillers occupy the terminal cells of the selected planter path. Default is FALSE. max_fillers Maximum number of filler plots considered when dimensions are selected automatically. When NULL, up to 10 filler plots are considered. year (optional) Year recorded in the YEAR column of the field book. By default the current year. rowcol_penalty Weight of the rule that keeps the copies of a replicated entry in distinct rows and columns (Williams et al., 2011; Cullis et al., 2006); see swap_pairs. The default 0 leaves every layout unchanged; Inf puts distinct rows and columns first. With the rule on, infoDesign$shared_pairs gives the pairs of copies that still share a row or column at each location. Turning it on changes the optimizer's random draws, so with several locations the later locations' layouts change as well. It needs spread_reps = TRUE. rowcol_scope "pairs" (default) covers the entries with exactly two copies; "all" also covers the checks and any entry with more copies.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list of class FielDHub with several elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • layoutRandom is a matrix with the randomization layout.

  • plotNumber is a matrix with the layout plot number.

  • binaryField is a matrix with the binary field.

  • fillerField is a logical matrix identifying filler plots.

  • dataEntry is a data frame with the data input.

  • genEntries is a list with the entries for replicated and non-replicated parts.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with field book design. This includes the index (Row, Column).

  • min_pairwise_distance is a data frame with the minimum pairwise distance between each pair of locations.

  • reps_info is a data frame with information on the number of replicated and non-replicated treatments at each location.

  • pairsDistance is a data frame with the pairwise distances between each pair of treatments.

  • treatments_with_reps is a list with the entries for the replicated part of the design.

  • treatments_with_no_reps is a list with the entries for the non-replicated part of the design.

  • list_locs is a list with each location list of entries.

  • multi_location_data is a data frame with the entries of every location: LOCATION | ENTRY | NAME | REPS.

  • allocation is a matrix with the allocation of treatments.

  • size_locations is a named vector with the size of each location.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: The allocation of entries to locations comes from do_optim(); see its Details for the search, and for allocations that changed in FielDHub 1.7.0.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(multi_location_prep, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Williams, E., Piepho, H.-P., & Whitaker, D. (2011). Augmented p-rep designs. Biometrical Journal, 53(1), 19-27. https://doi.org/10.1002/bimj.201000102

Cullis, B. R., Smith, A. B., & Coombes, N. E. (2006). On the design of early generation variety trials with correlated data. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 11, 381-393. https://doi.org/10.1198/108571106X154443

Edmondson, R.N. Multi-level Block Designs for Comparative Experiments. JABES 25, 500–522 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1007/s13253-020-00416-0

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Jean-Marc Montpetit [ctb], Ana Heilman [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Example 1: Generates a spatially optimized multi-location p-rep design with 142
# genotypes. The number of copies per plant available for this experiment is 9.
# This experiment is carried out in 5 locations, and there are seven seeds available
# for each plant to make replications.
# In this case, we add three controls (checks) with six reps each.
# With this setup, the experiment will have 142 treatments + 3 checks = 145
# entries and the number of plots per location after the allocation process
# will be 196.
# The average genotype allocation will be 1.5 copies per location.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
optim_multi_prep <- multi_location_prep(
  lines = 150,
  l = 5,
  copies_per_entry = 7,
  checks = 3,
  rep_checks = c(6,6,6),
  locationNames = c("LOC1", "LOC2", "LOC3", "LOC4", "LOC5"),
  seed = 1234
)
field_book <- optim_multi_prep$fieldBook
head(subset(field_book, LOCATION == "LOC1"), 10)
} # }

docs.title: Generates an Spatial Un-replicated Optimized Arrangement Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_optimized_arrangement.R

Randomly generates a spatial un-replicated optimized arrangement design, where the distance between checks is maximized in such a way that each row and column have control plots. Note that design generation needs the dimension of the field (number of rows and columns).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
optimized_arrangement(
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  lines = NULL,
  amountChecks = NULL,
  checks = NULL,
  planter = "serpentine",
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  seed = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  spread_reps = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  rep_checks = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: nrows Number of rows in the field. ncols Number of columns in the field. lines Number of genotypes, experimental lines or treatments. amountChecks Deprecated alias for rep_checks. checks Number of genotypes as checks. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. exptName (optional) Name of the experiment. locationNames (optional) Name for each location. spread_reps A logical value indicating whether to maximize the spatial distance between replicated treatments in the field. Default is TRUE. data (optional) Data frame with 3 columns: ENTRY | NAME | REPS. year (optional) Year recorded in the YEAR column of the field book. By default the current year. rep_checks Integer with the total amount of checks, or a numeric vector with the replicates of each check label.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with five elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • layoutRandom is a matrix with the randomization layout.

  • plotNumber is a matrix with the layout plot number.

  • dataEntry is a data frame with the data input.

  • genEntries is a list with the entries for replicated and no replicated part.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with field book design. This includes the index (Row, Column).

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(optimized_arrangement, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Clarke, G. P. Y., & Stefanova, K. T. (2011). Optimal design for early-generation plant breeding trials with unreplicated or partially replicated test lines. Australian & New Zealand Journal of Statistics, 53(4), 461–480.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Example 1: Generates a spatial unreplicated optimized arrangement design in one location
# with 120 genotypes + 20 check plots (4 checks) for a field with dimension 14 rows x 10 cols.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
optim_unrep1 <- optimized_arrangement(
  nrows = 14, 
  ncols = 10, 
  lines = 120,
  rep_checks = 20,
  checks = 1:4,
  planter = "cartesian", 
  plotNumber = 101,
  exptName = "20RW1",
  locationNames = "CASSELTON",
  seed = 14124
)
optim_unrep1$infoDesign
optim_unrep1$layoutRandom
optim_unrep1$plotNumber
head(optim_unrep1$fieldBook, 12)
} # }

# Example 2: Generates a spatial unreplicated optimized arrangement design in one location
# with 200 genotypes + 20 check plots (4 checks) for a field with dimension 10 rows x 22 cols.
# As example, we set up the data option with the entries list.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
checks <- 4
list_checks <- paste("CH", 1:checks, sep = "")
treatments <- paste("G", 5:204, sep = "")
REPS <- c(5, 5, 5, 5, rep(1, 200))
treatment_list <- data.frame(list(ENTRY = 1:204, NAME = c(list_checks, treatments), REPS = REPS))
head(treatment_list, 12) 
tail(treatment_list, 12)
optim_unrep2 <- optimized_arrangement(
  nrows = 10, 
  ncols = 22, 
  planter = "serpentine", 
  plotNumber = 101,
  seed = 120,
  exptName = "20YWA2",
  locationNames = "MINOT",
  data = treatment_list
)
optim_unrep2$infoDesign
optim_unrep2$layoutRandom
optim_unrep2$plotNumber
head(optim_unrep2$fieldBook,12)
} # }

docs.title: Generates a Spatial Partially Replicated Arrangement Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_partially_replicated.R

Randomly generates a spatial partially replicated (p-rep) design for single or multiple locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
partially_replicated(
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  repGens = NULL,
  repUnits = NULL,
  planter = "serpentine",
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  spread_reps = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  multiLocationData = FALSE,
  dist_method = "euclidean",
  border_penalization = 0.5,
  data = NULL,
  allow_fillers = FALSE,
  year = NULL,
  rowcol_penalty = 0,
  rowcol_scope = "pairs"
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: nrows Numeric vector with the number of rows field at each location. ncols Numeric vector with the number of columns field at each location. repGens Numeric vector with the amount genotypes to replicate. repUnits Numeric vector with the number of reps of each genotype. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian movement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. spread_reps A logical value indicating whether to maximize the spatial distance between replicated treatments in the field. Default is TRUE. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. exptName (optional) Name of the experiment. locationNames (optional) Name for each location. multiLocationData (optional) Option to pass an entry list for multiple locations. dist_method The method used for distance calculation. Options are "euclidean" (default) and "manhattan". By default multiLocationData = FALSE. border_penalization A tuning parameter for the centrality penalty. Default is 0.5. data (optional) Data frame with 3 columns: ENTRY | NAME | REPS. If multiLocationData = TRUE then the data must have 4 columns: LOCATION | ENTRY | NAME | REPS allow_fillers A logical value indicating whether field dimensions may exceed the number of experimental plots. Fillers occupy the terminal cells of the selected planter path. Default is FALSE. year (optional) Year recorded in the YEAR column of the field book. By default the current year. rowcol_penalty Weight of the rule that keeps the copies of a replicated entry in distinct rows and columns (Williams et al., 2011; Cullis et al., 2006); see swap_pairs. The default 0 leaves every layout unchanged; Inf puts distinct rows and columns first. With the rule on, infoDesign$shared_pairs gives the pairs of copies that still share a row or column at each location. Turning it on changes the optimizer's random draws, so with several locations the later locations' layouts change as well. It needs spread_reps = TRUE. rowcol_scope "pairs" (default) covers the entries with exactly two copies; "all" also covers the checks and any entry with more copies.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with several elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • layoutRandom is a matrix with the randomization layout.

  • plotNumber is a matrix with the layout plot number.

  • binaryField is a matrix with the binary field.

  • fillerField is a logical matrix identifying filler plots.

  • dataEntry is a data frame with the data input.

  • genEntries is a list with the entries for replicated and non-replicated parts.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with field book design. This includes the index (Row, Column).

  • min_pairwise_distance is a data frame with the minimum pairwise distance between each pair of locations.

  • reps_info is a data frame with information on the number of replicated and non-replicated treatments at each location.

  • pairsDistance is a data frame with the pairwise distances between each pair of treatments.

  • treatments_with_reps is a list with the entries for the replicated part of the design.

  • treatments_with_no_reps is a list with the entries for the non-replicated part of the design.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: This function generates and optimizes a partially replicated (p-rep) experimental design for a given set of treatments and replication levels. The design is represented by a matrix and optimized using a pairwise distance metric. The function outputs various information about the optimized design including the field layout, replicated and unreplicated treatments, and pairwise distances between treatments. Note that the design generation needs the dimension of the field (number of rows and columns).

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(partially_replicated, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Williams, E., Piepho, H.-P., & Whitaker, D. (2011). Augmented p-rep designs. Biometrical Journal, 53(1), 19-27. https://doi.org/10.1002/bimj.201000102

Cullis, B. R., Smith, A. B., & Coombes, N. E. (2006). On the design of early generation variety trials with correlated data. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 11, 381–393. https://doi.org/10.1198/108571106X154443

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Jean-Marc Montpetit [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Example 1: Generates a spatial optimized partially replicated arrangement design in one 
# location with 335 genotypes for a field with dimensions 15 rows x 28 cols. 
# Note that there are 250 genotypes unreplicated (only one time), 85 genotypes replicated 
# two times, and three checks 8 times each.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
prep_deseign1 <- partially_replicated(
 nrows = 12, 
 ncols = 37,  
 repGens = c(250, 85, 3),
 repUnits = c(1, 2, 8),
 planter = "cartesian", 
 plotNumber = 101,
 seed = 77
)
prep_deseign1$infoDesign
prep_deseign1$layoutRandom
prep_deseign1$plotNumber
head(prep_deseign1$fieldBook, 12)
} # }

# Example 2: Generates a spatial optimized partially replicated arrangement design with 492 
# genotypes in a field with dimensions 30 rows x 20 cols. Note that there 384 genotypes 
# unreplicated (only one time), 108 genotypes replicated two times. 
# In this case we don't have check plots.
# As example, we set up the data option with the entries list.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
NAME <- paste("G", 1:492, sep = "")
repGens = c(108, 384);repUnits = c(2,1)
REPS <- rep(repUnits, repGens)
treatment_list <- data.frame(list(ENTRY = 1:492, NAME = NAME, REPS = REPS))
head(treatment_list, 12) 
tail(treatment_list, 12)
prep_deseign2 <- partially_replicated(
  nrows = 30, 
  ncols = 20, 
  planter = "serpentine", 
  plotNumber = 101,
  seed = 41,
  data = treatment_list
)
prep_deseign2$infoDesign
prep_deseign2$layoutRandom
prep_deseign2$plotNumber
head(prep_deseign2$fieldBook, 10)
} # }

docs.title: Plot a FielDHub object
docs.text:
Source: R/result_methods.R

Draw a field layout plot for a FielDHub object.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# S3 method for class 'FielDHub'
plot(x, ...)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
x a object inheriting from class FielDHub ...

further arguments passed to utility function plot_layout().

  • layout a integer. Options available depend on the type of design and its characteristics

  • l a integer to specify the location to plot.

  • planter it can be serpentine or cartesian. It has no effect on split-plot and split-split-plot designs in complete blocks (type = 2), whose whole plots are numbered in a fixed order.

  • stacked it can be vertical or horizontal stacked layout.

  • nrows, ncols the rows and columns of a field grid, as in field_layout(); they cannot be combined with layout. With them, stacked arranges the replicates in that field ("vertical", "horizontal" or "grid_panel"); when it is not given, the stacking whose replicate is the most square is drawn. A design built with nrows or ncols draws only that grid: another planter or stacked is an error.

  • field_grid FALSE removes the white line drawn around every plot in maps that have one. Other arguments are passed to desplot.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
• a plot object inheriting from class fieldLayout

  • field_book a data frame with the fieldbook that includes the coordinates ROW and COLUMN.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Plot a RCBD design with 24 treatments and 3 reps.
s <- RCBD(t = 24, reps = 3, plotNumber = 101, seed = 12)
plot(s)
} # }

docs.title: Read a validated recorded design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_read_design.R

Read a validated recorded design

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: read_design(file, format = "rds")

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: file Local filename. Only read serialized files from trusted sources. format Explicit format key from design_formats(); currently "rds" is the lossless import format.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: The complete saved result, unchanged. File/format input mistakes raise fieldhub_input_error; corrupt or incompatible contents raise fieldhub_import_error, with the original condition in parent.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Imports validate the result schema, recorded parameters and known engine. They do not randomize, reconstruct a design, or execute an R script. Unknown schema versions are rejected, not silently coerced. Pre-metadata legacy objects remain usable through readRDS() but do not contain the recorded-input contract required by this importer.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
x <- RCBD(t = 5, reps = 3, seed = 27)
write_design(x, file)
identical(read_design(file), x)
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(file)

docs.title: Generates a Rectangular Lattice Design.
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_rectangular_lattice.R

It randomly generates a rectangular lattice design across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
rectangular_lattice(
  t = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  locationNames = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments, or a character vector with the treatment labels. k Size of incomplete blocks (number of units per incomplete block). r Deprecated alias for reps; positional calls remain supported. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. reps Number of full resolvable replicates per location. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the serpentine planting path of the whole field. See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the rectangular lattice design field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters, using reps for replication. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(rectangular_lattice, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]
