docs.title: Reconstruct a design from its recorded inputs
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_reproduce_design.R

Calls the design engine using the input parameters and random-number settings recorded in a result's metadata.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: reproduce_design(x)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: x A FielDHub design, allocation plan, or pair-swap optimization result with recorded parameters.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A newly generated design or allocation plan, invisibly.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The caller's RNG settings and .Random.seed are restored on exit, including when reconstruction fails. Arguments are passed as values, so language objects in the parameter list are not evaluated as code.

Reproduction requires the same software versions and platform for algorithms whose results depend on numerical optimization. A different FielDHub version signals a fieldhub_reproduction_warning; dependency or platform differences are not checked. Older results without recorded parameters cannot be reconstructed automatically, but remain usable for printing and plotting.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
x <- RCBD(t = 5, reps = 3, seed = 38)
identical(reproduce_design(x), x)
#> [1] TRUE

docs.title: Reconstruct recorded simulated responses
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_reproduce_simulation.R

Replays a design-based Gaussian, classic truncated-normal or spatial AR1-by-AR1 simulation using its saved input field book, parameters, seed, and RNG settings.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: reproduce_simulation(x)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: x A simulation record containing input_field_book, field_book, and metadata. Metadata must contain model, schema_version, seed, rng_kind, package_version, and the named parameters used by that model.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: The reconstructed simulation record, invisibly.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
This reconstructs the responses, not the experimental design or its layout: it starts from the exact saved input field book. Use reproduce_design() separately to reconstruct the experimental design. The caller's RNG settings and .Random.seed are restored on exit. R cannot save the normal value that Box-Muller holds in reserve, so when the caller uses Box-Muller normals, replaying a record made under another normal generator discards that reserved value and the caller's next rnorm() draw differs. Records made by simulate() under Box-Muller use a private stream and leave it untouched. Recorded arguments are passed as values rather than evaluated as R code. A changed FielDHub version signals a fieldhub_reproduction_warning; reproduction across software versions or platforms is not guaranteed.

Spatial min_value and max_value determine the model's center and genetic-effect scale, not hard response bounds. Spatial records retain unrounded per-location simulation values separately from the field book, whose responses are rounded to two decimal places. Classic records use a truncated-normal model, with rounding also applied to the field book.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: reproduce_design()

docs.title: Generates a Resolvable Row-Column Design (RowColD)
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_row_column.R

It randomly generates a resolvable row-column design (RowColD). The design is optimized in both rows and columns blocking factors. The randomization can be done across multiple locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
row_column(
  t = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  locationNames = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  iterations = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  method = c("onestage", "twostage"),
  latinize = FALSE,
  reps = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments, or a character vector with the treatment labels. nrows Number of rows of a full resolvable replicate. r Deprecated alias for reps; positional calls remain supported. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. iterations Finite positive whole-number optimization budget, at most .Machine$integer.max. Its meaning and default depend on method. For method = "onestage" it is the effort of the joint stage only: the number of joint searches is max(1, round(10 * iterations / 200)), so the default 200 runs 10 joint searches and values up to 29 run one. The first stage (the row search and the columns within the rows) and the repair of a singular joint model always run in full, whatever iterations is. On large designs the work cap of the search ends it before that many joint searches have run, so iterations is then an upper limit on their number. For method = "twostage" it is the effort of the row search: its default evaluation budget is scaled by iterations / 1000, so the default 1000 is the full search, smaller values stop it earlier (1 is the smallest effort) and larger values allow a longer search. It does not change the column design. If NULL (the default), a value appropriate to the chosen method is used. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments method Optimization strategy for the row and column blocking factors. Either "onestage" (default) or "twostage". With "onestage" (also known as simultaneous) FielDHub's block engine searches the rows first and then improves the joint row-by-column D-criterion without lowering the row efficiencies, which usually yields a higher joint row-by-column A-Efficiency (see Details and the Row-by-Column row of blocksModel); iterations sets the effort of its joint stage. With "twostage" the columns are optimized first, as blocks nested in replicates, by FielDHub's own block engine, and the rows are then improved by the same engine, keeping the columns fixed. "onestage" falls back to "twostage", with one warning, for very small designs whose joint model has too few residual degrees of freedom (or where no full-rank joint design was found), so "twostage" rarely has to be requested explicitly. latinize If TRUE, optimize the row and column blocking factors as crossed (latinized) effects shared across the replicates, so that each treatment tends to appear in different rows and columns across the replicates. By default FALSE. Only meaningful with method = "onestage"; it is ignored for method = "twostage" (which cannot latinize across replicates), where passing latinize = TRUE is ignored with a warning. If method = "onestage" falls back to "twostage" (see Details), the returned design is not latinized and the warning says so. reps Number of full resolvable replicates per location.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with five elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters. For an onestage design it includes joint_searches, a list with requested, the number of joint searches iterations asks for, and completed, one number per location: the joint searches that ran to their own end, not cut short by the work cap of the search. It is absent when the result is a twostage design.

  • blocksModel is a list (one element per location) with the efficiency of the design. In addition to the per-factor Rep, Row and Column A- and D-Efficiencies, it reports a Row-by-Column row with the joint A- and D-Efficiency of the standard resolvable row-column analysis model (rows and columns adjusted together).

  • resolvableBlocks a list with the resolvable row columns blocks.

  • concurrence is the concurrence matrix.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the row-column field book.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
With method = "twostage", the Row-Column design is built in two stages. The first step constructs the blocking factor Columns using Incomplete Block Units from an incomplete block design that sets the number of incomplete blocks as the number of Columns in the design, each of which has a dimension equal to the number of Rows. Once this design is generated, the Rows are used as the Row blocking factor, which is optimized while the Columns are kept fixed. To optimize the Rows while keeping the optimized Columns, FielDHub's block engine treats the rows of each replicate as incomplete blocks and searches over swaps of two plots of the same Column in different Rows, so every column keeps its treatments and every replicate holds each treatment once. Starting from the column design, it accepts swaps that improve the row blocks' D-criterion until no single swap improves it, then tries a few random escapes from that local optimum. The iterations argument sets the effort of this row search (see iterations). Earlier versions of FielDHub improved the rows with random greedy swaps instead, so their seeded "twostage" layouts differ.

When method = "onestage" (the default, also called simultaneous), the rows and columns are optimized together by FielDHub's block engine, in stages. First the rows are searched on their own, as incomplete blocks within each replicate, and the columns are then arranged within the rows without changing them. A joint stage then improves the joint row-by-column D-criterion of the standard analysis model (rows and columns adjusted together) with swaps of two plots of the same replicate, accepting a swap only if it does not lower the row efficiencies reached in the first stage; a first-stage design whose joint model is singular is repaired before this stage. Several joint searches are run, each from its own first-stage design; of those that end with a joint model of full rank, the one with the best row D- and A-Efficiency, and then the best joint D-Efficiency, is returned. The joint row-by-column A-Efficiency is reported as the Row-by-Column row of blocksModel. With the default latinize = FALSE the rows and columns are nested within the replicates, the criterion that "twostage" also uses, and the joint efficiency is typically higher than with "twostage"; with latinize = TRUE the rows and columns are shared across replicates (see below). The size of the joint gain is layout-dependent and tends to be largest for small designs with few replicates. For method = "onestage", iterations sets the effort of the joint stage only (see iterations).

method = "onestage" falls back to method = "twostage" with a single warning, rather than failing, so a design is still produced, when the joint row-and-column model has too few residual degrees of freedom to estimate every treatment comparison (very small designs), or no joint search found a design whose joint model has full rank. The fallback design is a nested twostage design: with latinize = TRUE the warning says that the returned design is not latinized.

No design is refused for its size. The work of the onestage search is capped instead: once the cap is spent the search stops and returns the design it holds. On large designs it is therefore the cap, not iterations, that sets the number of joint searches, and infoDesign$joint_searches reports the number asked for and the number that ran to their end. The result is still an optimized onestage design, with the rows and columns coded as requested, and it is reproducible from the seed; no warning is given for it. Only for designs beyond about 2000 treatments (fewer with more than four replicates), whose joint search cannot be started at all, does row_column() give one warning: it then returns an onestage design in which the rows, and the columns within the rows, were optimized as far as their own searches could be started, and says which.

Setting latinize = TRUE (only available with method = "onestage") codes the rows and columns as crossed blocking factors shared across the replicates, so that a treatment tends to occupy different rows and different columns in the different replicates (a latinized resolvable row-column design in the sense of John and Williams). This guards against the same treatment recurring in the same field row or column over the whole trial, not just within a replicate, and is useful when a field trend runs along the whole-field rows or columns. It optimizes a different (crossed) model than the default nested one, so the two are not directly comparable, and full latinization is only possible when there are at least as many rows and columns as replicates. By default (latinize = FALSE) the rows and columns stay nested within each replicate. latinize has no effect for method = "twostage", which cannot latinize across replicates.

docs.title: Run the Shiny Application
docs.text:
Source: R/run_app.R

Run the Shiny Application

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: run_app(..., launch.browser = TRUE, workers = 0L)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: ... Unused, for extensibility launch.browser Logical. If `TRUE`, the application is launched in the system's default web browser. workers Non-negative integer. Background workers; the default 0L keeps synchronous execution and does not start any worker processes.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A shiny app object

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Constructing the app does not change R options. On startup, uploads are limited to 100 MiB (100 * 1024^2 bytes); when the app stops, the previous upload-limit option is restored, including an unset option. Shiny uses a process-wide upload limit, shared by the app's sessions while it is running. Closing one session does not restore the limit for others.

The standard app packages are installed with FielDHub. If any are unavailable, this function signals a fieldhub_dependency_error with an installation command and the missing package names in its packages field. It never installs packages automatically. Only the background-worker backend is optional.

With workers > 0, an installed package and the optional mirai package run design jobs in a private background pool. Other sessions remain responsive while a design runs. The pool closes when the app stops. Without mirai, or with development source, execution stays synchronous with a message.

docs.title: Simulate a continuous trait on a FielDHub design
docs.text:
Source: R/sim_design.R

Generate Gaussian plot responses using the treatment and experimental units of the realized randomization. Repeated entries, including checks, share a treatment effect across plots and locations. Each draw generates new random effects. Filler plots remain in the field book with missing responses.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# S3 method for class 'FielDHub'
simulate(
  object,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  ...,
  trait = "YIELD",
  mean = 100,
  residual_sd = 8,
  treatment_sd = NULL,
  design_sd = NULL,
  location_sd = NULL,
  spatial = FALSE
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: object A FielDHub field design. nsim Positive number of independent trials to draw. seed Simulation seed. With NULL, one seed is drawn and recorded. If R is using Box-Muller normals, simulation draws from a private stream to preserve the caller's cached normal. ... Reserved for future extensions. trait Name of the response column for one draw. Multiple draws use this name with a numeric suffix. mean Trait mean, or a named vector giving the mean for each location. residual_sd Nonnegative plot-error standard deviation, or a named vector giving the standard deviation for each location. treatment_sd Nonnegative standard deviation of the treatment signal. The default is 1.25 times the typical residual SD. For factorial treatments, its variance is divided equally among the main effects and a combination-specific interaction. design_sd Nonnegative standard deviation for each design term, or a named vector overriding specific terms. Omitted terms use half the typical residual SD. location_sd Standard deviation of independent location shifts when mean is a single unnamed value and the trial has several locations. Defaults to 0.625 times the typical residual SD. spatial FALSE (default), TRUE for defaults, or a named list overriding sd (half the typical residual SD), rho_row (0.5) and rho_col (0.5). The spatial effect is a separable AR1 x AR1 field with standard deviation sd: rho_row is the correlation between plots in adjacent rows of the same column, rho_col between plots in adjacent columns of the same row, and plots dr rows and dc columns apart have correlation rho_row^dr * rho_col^dc. Spatial correlation requires physical ROW and COLUMN in the field book, with unique coordinate pairs within each location. A Latin square or row-column design stores its experimental rows and columns there, so first replace its field book with the physical layout: x$fieldBook <- field_layout(x), then simulate(x, spatial = TRUE). The layout keeps the experimental axes as ROW_SQ/COLUMN_SQ or ROW_REP/COLUMN_REP, so the design effects are unchanged.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: A fieldhub_simulation list with the field book augmented by the responses, the input field book, the response data frame, one list of plot-aligned effect contributions per draw, and replay metadata. Standard deviations are in trait units and the Gaussian response is unbounded.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: The typical residual SD is the arithmetic mean of the location residual SDs. These defaults scale the trait signal and the effects of the design when the user changes the residual SD to suit a trait's units.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: reproduce_simulation()

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
x <- RCBD(t = 6, reps = 3, nrows = 3, seed = 20)
sim <- stats::simulate(x, seed = 42, mean = 6, residual_sd = 0.4,
                       treatment_sd = 0.6, design_sd = 0.3)
head(sim$field_book)
#>   ID LOCATION PLOT ROW COLUMN REP TREATMENT    YIELD
#> 1  1     loc1  101   1      1   1        T6 6.364696
#> 2  2     loc1  102   1      2   1        T3 7.193282
#> 3  3     loc1  206   2      1   1        T4 7.747832
#> 4  4     loc1  205   2      2   1        T2 5.559093
#> 5  5     loc1  301   3      1   1        T1 7.164516
#> 6  6     loc1  302   3      2   1        T5 6.642689

# Spatial simulation of a row-column design on its physical layout
rc <- row_column(t = 12, nrows = 3, reps = 2, seed = 1)
rc$fieldBook <- field_layout(rc)
sim_rc <- stats::simulate(rc, seed = 7, spatial = list(rho_row = 0.6, rho_col = 0.3))
sim_rc
#> FielDHub trait simulation (design_gaussian)
#>   Plots: 24  Locations: 1  Draws: 1  Seed: 7

docs.title: Unreplicated designs using the sparse allocation approach
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_sparse_allocation.R

Unreplicated designs using the sparse allocation approach

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
sparse_allocation(
  lines,
  nrows,
  ncols,
  l,
  planter = "serpentine",
  plotNumber,
  copies_per_entry,
  checks = NULL,
  exptName = NULL,
  locationNames,
  sparse_list,
  seed,
  data = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  checksPercent = NULL,
  spread_checks = FALSE,
  dist_method = "euclidean"
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: lines Number of genotypes, experimental lines or treatments. nrows Number of rows in the field. ncols Number of columns in the field. l Number of locations or sites. By default l = 1. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian plot arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. copies_per_entry Number of copies per plant. When design is sparse then copies_per_entry \< l checks Number of genotypes checks. exptName (optional) Name of the experiment. locationNames (optional) Names each location. sparse_list (optional) A class "Sparse" object generated by do_optim() function. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. data (optional) Data frame with 2 columns: ENTRY | NAME. ENTRY must be numeric. year (optional) Year recorded in the YEAR column of the field book. By default the current year. checksPercent (optional) Percentage of checks in each location, one of the options available for the field. By default the last (largest) option. spread_checks Logical. Exchange check identities among the existing check plots of each location to increase separation of repeated checks, as in diagonal_arrangement(). The allocation of entries to locations, test entries, filler plots, the check plots themselves and each check's replication in a location stay fixed. The default FALSE preserves the original randomization. dist_method Distance between field coordinates for check optimization: "euclidean" (default) or "manhattan". Grid steps have equal scale.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with nine elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters. With check optimization enabled, check_optimization records the search of each location.

  • check_spacing records the same-check spacing of each location (see diagonal_arrangement()), before and, with optimization enabled, after the search.

  • layoutRandom is a list with the randomization layout of each location.

  • plotsNumber is a list with the plot number layout of each location.

  • data_entry is a data frame with the data input.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the field book of all locations.

  • list_locs is a list with each location list of entries.

  • allocation is a matrix with the allocation of treatments.

  • size_locations is a named vector with the number of lines allocated to each location.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The allocation of entries to locations comes from do_optim(); see its Details for the search, and for allocations that changed in FielDHub 1.7.0.

Check optimization is the deterministic local exchange described in diagonal_arrangement(), run in each location on its own. It measures spacing, not statistical precision.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(sparse_allocation, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Edmondson, R.N. Multi-level Block Designs for Comparative Experiments. JABES 25, 500–522 (2020). https://doi.org/10.1007/s13253-020-00416-0

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
sparse <- sparse_allocation(
  lines = 120,
  l = 4,
  copies_per_entry = 3,
  checks = 4,
  locationNames = c("LOC1", "LOC2", "LOC3", "LOC4"),
  seed = 1234
)

docs.title: Split a population of genotypes randomly into several locations.
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_split_families.R

Split a population of genotypes randomly into several locations, with the aim of having approximatelly the same number of replicates of each genotype, line or treatment per location.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: split_families(l = NULL, data = NULL, seed = NULL)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: l Number of locations. data Data frame with the entry (ENTRY) and the labels of each treatment (NAME) and number of individuals per family group (FAMILY). seed (optional) A single real number specifying the random seed. When omitted, one integer is drawn from the current random-number stream and recorded in infoDesign$seed and metadata$seed; the allocation's own randomization does not change the caller's stream.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • rowsEachlist is a table with a summary of cases.

  • data_locations is a data frame with the entries for each location

docs.title: Details
docs.text: To reproduce an allocation previously made with set.seed(s); split_families(l, data), use split_families(l, data, seed = s).

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(split_families, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Generates a Split Plot Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_split_plot.R

It randomly generates a split plot design (SPD) across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
split_plot(
  wp = NULL,
  sp = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  type = 2,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  seed = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  factorLabels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: wp Number of whole plots, as an integer or a vector. sp Number of sub plots per whole plot, as an integer or a vector. reps Number of blocks (full replicates). type Option for CRD or RCBD designs. Values are type = 1 (CRD) or type = 2 (RCBD). By default type = 2. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. factorLabels (optional) If TRUE retain the levels labels from the original data set otherwise, numeric labels will be assigned. Default is factorLabels =TRUE. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the serpentine planting path of the whole field. See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout. An error for type = 1, which has no replicates to stack.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the split plot field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(split_plot, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Federer, W. T. (1955). Experimental Design. Theory and Application. New York, USA. The Macmillan Company.

docs.title: Author

docs.title: Generates a Split Split Plot Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_split_split_plot.R

It randomly generates a split split plot design (SSPD) across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
split_split_plot(
  wp = NULL,
  sp = NULL,
  ssp = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  type = 2,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  seed = NULL,
  locationNames = NULL,
  factorLabels = TRUE,
  data = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: wp Number of whole plots, as an integer or a vector. sp Number of sub plots per whole plot, as an integer or a vector. ssp Number of sub-sub plots, as an integer or a vector. reps Number of blocks (full replicates). type Option for CRD or RCBD designs. Values are type = 1 (CRD) or type = 2 (RCBD). By default type = 2. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. factorLabels (optional) If TRUE retain the levels labels from the original data set otherwise, numeric labels will be assigned. Default is factorLabels =TRUE. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the serpentine planting path of the whole field. See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout. An error for type = 1, which has no replicates to stack.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the split split plot field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(split_split_plot, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Federer, W. T. (1955). Experimental Design. Theory and Application. New York, USA. The Macmillan Company.

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Example 1: Generates a split split plot design SSPD with 5 whole plots, 2 sub-plots,
# 3 sub-sub plots, and 3 reps in an RCBD arrangement. This is for one location.
SSPD1 <- split_split_plot(wp = 4, sp = 2, ssp = 3, reps = 5, l = 1, 
                          plotNumber = 101, 
                          seed = 23, 
                          type = 2, 
                          locationNames = "FARGO")

# Example 2: Generates a split split plot design SSPD with 2 whole plost 
# (Irrigation, No irrigation), 5 sub plots (4 types of fungicide + one control), and 
# 10 sub-sub plots (Ten varieties of beans), and 4 reps in an RCBD arrangement.
# This is for 3 locations. In this case, we show how to use the option data.
wp <- paste("IRR_", c("NO", "Yes"), sep = "") #Irrigation (2 Whole plots)

split_split_plot_Data <- data.frame(list(WHOLPLOT = c(wp, rep(NA, 8)), 
                                         SUBPLOT = c(sp, rep(NA, 5)),
                                         SUB_SUBPLOTS = ssp))

docs.title: Generates a Square Lattice Design.
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_square_lattice.R

It randomly generates a square lattice design across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
square_lattice(
  t = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = 101,
  locationNames = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  reps = NULL,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: t Number of treatments, or a character vector with the treatment labels. k Size of incomplete blocks (number of units per incomplete block). r Deprecated alias for reps; positional calls remain supported. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. data (optional) Data frame with label list of treatments. reps Number of full resolvable replicates per location. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the serpentine planting path of the whole field. See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with two elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the square lattice design field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters, using reps for replication. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(square_lattice, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: Author
docs.text: Didier Murillo [aut], Salvador Gezan [aut], Ana Heilman [ctb], Thomas Walk [ctb], Johan Aparicio [ctb], Richard Horsley [ctb]

docs.title: Strip Plot Design
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_strip_plot.R

It randomly generates a strip plot design across locations.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
strip_plot(
  Hplots = NULL,
  Vplots = NULL,
  b = 1,
  l = 1,
  plotNumber = NULL,
  planter = "serpentine",
  locationNames = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  factorLabels = TRUE,
  randomizeH = TRUE,
  randomizeV = FALSE,
  data = NULL,
  reps = 1,
  nrows = NULL,
  ncols = NULL,
  stacked = NULL
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Hplots Number of horizontal factors, as an integer or a vector. Vplots Number of vertical factors, as an integer or a vector. b Deprecated alias for reps; positional calls remain supported. l Number of locations. By default l = 1. plotNumber Numeric vector with the starting plot number for each location. By default plotNumber = 101. planter Option for serpentine or cartesian arrangement. By default planter = 'serpentine'. locationNames (optional) Names for each location. seed (optional) Real number that specifies the starting seed to obtain reproducible designs. factorLabels (optional) If TRUE retain the levels labels from the original data set otherwise, numeric labels will be assigned. Default is factorLabels =TRUE. randomizeH Logical flag: TRUE to randomize horizontal strips separately in each replicate; FALSE to randomize once per location and reuse. randomizeV Logical flag: TRUE to randomize vertical strips separately in each replicate; FALSE to randomize once per location and reuse. data (optional) data frame with the labels of vertical and horizontal plots. reps Number of blocks (full replicates) per location. Default is one. nrows, ncols Optional positive whole numbers: the rows and columns of the field at each location. If only one is given, the other follows from the number of plots. The field book then has ROW and COLUMN, and its plots are numbered along the planting path of the whole field (see planter). See field_layout for how the design is placed. stacked How the replicates of a field of given dimensions are arranged: "vertical" (one above another, each across all the columns of the field), "horizontal" (side by side, each down all its rows) or "grid_panel" (in rows and columns of replicates). It needs nrows or ncols. By default the arrangement whose replicate is the most square among those that fit the dimensions; the stacking chosen is recorded in the design. See field_layout.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list with four elements.

  • infoDesign is a list with information on the design parameters.

  • stripsBlockLoc is a list with the strip blocks for each location.

  • plotLayouts is a list with the layout plot numbers for each location.

  • fieldBook is a data frame with the strip plot field book.

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text: The result records effective inputs and the resolved seed in metadata$parameters. Under the same package versions and RNG settings, rebuild a result x with do.call(strip_plot, x$metadata$parameters).

docs.title: References
docs.text: Federer, W. T. (1955). Experimental Design. Theory and Application. New York, USA. The Macmillan Company.

docs.title: Swap pairs in a matrix of integers
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_swap_pairs.R

Attempts to separate repeated entries by swapping cells of different entries. Distance thresholds increase from starting_dist in steps of one. Candidate sampling, mean pairwise distance, and a centrality penalty guide the search. The last successful threshold layout is returned (with the row/column rule on, the successful layout with the fewest pairs of copies sharing a row or column; see rowcol_penalty); if none succeeds, the original matrix is returned. A requested minimum distance is not guaranteed.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
swap_pairs(
  X,
  starting_dist = 3,
  stop_iter = 10,
  lambda = 0.5,
  dist_method = "euclidean",
  candidate_sample_size = 4,
  seed = NULL,
  rowcol_penalty = 0,
  rowcol_scope = "pairs"
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: X A numeric matrix of whole-number entry identifiers within R's integer range. Missing cells are inactive positions and never move. starting_dist First distance threshold; a finite nonnegative number. Default is 3. stop_iter Maximum complete swap sweeps per threshold, as a nonnegative whole number within R's integer range. Default is 10. lambda Finite nonnegative weight for the centrality penalty. Default is 0.5. dist_method Coordinate distance used for candidate filtering, scoring, stopping, and reported distances: "euclidean" (default) or "manhattan". candidate_sample_size Maximum candidates evaluated per swap, as a positive whole number within R's integer range. Default is 4. seed Optional randomization seed. When omitted, one integer is drawn from the current random-number stream and recorded; the swap's own randomization does not change the caller's stream. rowcol_penalty Weight of the row/column rule: one number at least 0, or Inf. The default 0 turns the rule off and leaves every layout unchanged. When positive, the copies of a covered entry that share a row or a column are treated as a problem to fix even when they are far apart, and a candidate swap scores its distance score minus rowcol_penalty times the change in the number of shared pairs. Inf is strict: a swap that leaves fewer shared pairs always wins, and distance decides among equals (rows and columns first). With the rule on, the result keeps the successful threshold step with the fewest shared pairs (the largest threshold breaks ties), the search steps after it are dropped from designs, distances and rows_incidence, and diagnostics adds rowcol_penalty, rowcol_scope, retained_threshold, shared_pairs_input, shared_pairs_final and entries_sharing_final. rowcol_scope Entries the row/column rule covers: "pairs" (default), the entries with exactly two copies, or "all", every entry with two or more copies, checks included.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
A list containing:

optim_design The modified matrix. designs A list of the retained threshold layouts, starting from the input matrix; with the row/column rule on, it ends at the kept layout. distances A list of the pair distances of each layout in designs. min_distance The minimum distance between pairs of occurrences of the same integer in the final design. pairwise_distance A data frame with the pairwise distances for the final design. rows_incidence Row-repetition counts for retained threshold steps, or for the original matrix when no step succeeds. diagnostics The distance metric, stop reason, total completed sweeps (iterations), per-threshold budget, number of attempted thresholds, last threshold, last attempted minimum distance, and retained minimum distance. Stop reasons are iteration_limit, distance_range_complete, and no_distance_thresholds. A failed attempt is not retained in optim_design. metadata The design identifier, schema and package versions, RNG settings, resolved seed and complete input parameters, including X. The result inherits from fieldhub_optimization.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The finite threshold range is bounded by the field geometry. For Euclidean distance without missing cells, the historical bound is sqrt(nrow(X)^2 + ncol(X)^2); with missing cells it is the maximum distance between active positions. For Manhattan distance it is the maximum Manhattan distance between active positions. There are at most floor(bound - starting_dist) + 1 thresholds when the bound is at least starting_dist, and none otherwise. Each threshold permits at most stop_iter complete sweeps. Diagnostics distinguish an exhausted threshold budget from completing or skipping the distance range.

Standalone calls use the shared seed contract. To reproduce a previous set.seed(s); swap_pairs(X) call, with X already constructed, pass seed = s. Calls without a seed now select an automatic seed, so their layouts can differ from previous versions. Optimization performed inside field-design engines retains its existing draw sequence. Use reproduce_design() to replay a recorded optimization result.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
Williams, E., Piepho, H.-P., & Whitaker, D. (2011). Augmented p-rep designs. Biometrical Journal, 53(1), 19-27. https://doi.org/10.1002/bimj.201000102

Cullis, B. R., Smith, A. B., & Coombes, N. E. (2006). On the design of early generation variety trials with correlated data. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 11, 381-393. https://doi.org/10.1198/108571106X154443

docs.title: Write a recorded design or standalone replay script
docs.text:
Source: R/fct_write_design.R

Write a recorded design or standalone replay script

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: write_design(x, file, format = "rds", overwrite = FALSE)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: x A validated design, allocation or optimization result with recorded parameters. App-selected layouts and simulations are separate artifacts. file Local output filename; its parent directory must already exist. format Explicit exporter key from design_formats(): "rds" saves the exact result and metadata; "r" saves a standalone script assigning the reconstructed result to design. overwrite One logical value. Existing files are protected by default.

docs.title: Value
docs.text: file, invisibly. Unsupported formats and overwrite mistakes raise fieldhub_input_error; write failures raise fieldhub_export_error.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Serialization completes in a temporary file before the destination is copied. This protects an existing file from serialization failures, but is not an atomic filesystem transaction. Disk/copy failures still require normal backups. The temporary file is removed on exit.

R scripts embed only portable data and never evaluate recorded arguments during export. Large uploads or nonportable values require the RDS format. Reconstruction can depend on matching software versions and platform; the RDS format preserves the actual saved result independently of replay.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
write_design(CRD(t = 4, reps = 2, seed = 27), file)
read_design(file)$metadata
#> $design
#> [1] "crd"
#> 
#> $schema_version
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 27
#> 
#> $rng_kind
#> [1] "Mersenne-Twister" "Inversion"        "Rejection"       
#> 
#> $package_version
#> [1] "1.7.5"
#> 
#> $parameters
#> $parameters$t
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $parameters$reps
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $parameters$plotNumber
#> [1] 101
#> 
#> $parameters$seed
#> [1] 27
#> 
#> $parameters$data
